```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

BLUE = "#1976D2"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load and clean the data (every column is stored as text)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
raw = pd.read_csv("../data/melbourne-venues.csv")
for col in ["census_year", "number_of_seats", "latitude", "longitude"]:
    raw[col] = pd.to_numeric(raw[col], errors="coerce")
raw = raw.dropna(subset=["census_year"])
raw["census_year"] = raw["census_year"].astype(int)
raw["number_of_seats"] = raw["number_of_seats"].fillna(0)
raw["seat_type"] = raw["seating_type"].fillna("").str.contains("outdoor", case=False).map(
    {True: "Outdoor", False: "Indoor"}
)

# One row per venue per year (a venue can have indoor and outdoor rows)
venues = (
    raw.groupby(["census_year", "property_id", "trading_name"], as_index=False)
        .agg(
        area=("clue_small_area", "first"),
        latitude=("latitude", "first"),
        longitude=("longitude", "first"),
        seats=("number_of_seats", "sum"),
        industry=("industry_anzsic4_description", "first"),
    )
)

# Simplify area names: merge the two West Melbourne areas
venues["area"] = venues["area"].replace({
    "West Melbourne (Residential)": "West Melbourne",
    "West Melbourne (Industrial)": "West Melbourne",
    "Melbourne (Remainder)": "Melbourne (outside CBD)",
})

venues = venues[venues["area"] != "South Yarra"]   # no mappable venues in this area

# Group the 73 ANZSIC industry categories into interpretable venue types
TYPE_GROUPS = {
    "Restaurants": [
        "Cafes and Restaurants",
    ],
    "Takeaway": [
        "Takeaway Food Services", "Catering Services",
    ],
    "Bars": [
        "Pubs, Taverns and Bars", "Clubs (Hospitality)",
    ],
    "Hotels": [
        "Accommodation",
    ],
    "Food shops": [
        "Bakery Product Manufacturing (Non-factory based)",
        "Other Specialised Food Retailing", "Supermarket and Grocery Stores",
        "Convenience Store", "Fruit and Vegetable Retailing",
        "Fresh Meat, Fish and Poultry Retailing", "Liquor Retailing",
        "Other Food Product Manufacturing n.e.c.", "Cereal, Pasta and Baking Mix Manufacturing",
        "Fruit and Vegetable Wholesaling",
    ],
    "Entertainment, sport & culture": [
        "Sports and Physical Recreation Venues, Grounds and Facilities Operation",
        "Performing Arts Venue Operation", "Performing Arts Operation",
        "Other Gambling Activities", "Casino Operation",
        "Zoological and Botanical Gardens Operation",
        "Amusement and Other Recreational Activities n.e.c.", "Amusement Parks and Centres Operation",
        "Health and Fitness Centres and Gymnasia Operation",
        "Sports and Physical Recreation Clubs and Sports Professionals",
        "Sports and Physical Recreation Instruction",
        "Horse and Dog Racing Administration and Track Operation",
        "Museum Operation", "Motion Picture Exhibition",
    ],
}
# Turn the groups into a lookup: category -> type; anything not listed becomes "Other"
TYPE_OF = {cat: group for group, cats in TYPE_GROUPS.items() for cat in cats}
venues["type"] = venues["industry"].map(TYPE_OF).fillna("Other")

first_year = venues["census_year"].min()
latest_year = venues["census_year"].max()
latest = venues[venues["census_year"] == latest_year]
first = venues[venues["census_year"] == first_year]

n_latest = len(latest)
n_first = len(first)
change_n = n_latest - n_first
change_pct = change_n / n_first * 100

seats_latest = raw.loc[raw["census_year"] == latest_year]
total_seats = seats_latest["number_of_seats"].sum()
outdoor_share = (
    seats_latest.loc[seats_latest["seat_type"] == "Outdoor", "number_of_seats"].sum()
    / total_seats * 100
)
indoor_share = 100 - outdoor_share

# Survival: share of venues open 10 years before the latest census that are still open
years = sorted(venues["census_year"].unique())
base_year = max(y for y in years if y <= latest_year - 10)
key = ["property_id", "trading_name"]
base_keys = set(map(tuple, venues.loc[venues["census_year"] == base_year, key].values))
latest_keys = set(map(tuple, latest[key].values))
survival_pct = len(base_keys & latest_keys) / len(base_keys) * 100

# Fastest-growing area since the first census (areas with at least 20 venues at the start)
counts = venues.groupby(["area", "census_year"]).size().unstack()
start, end = counts[first_year], counts[latest_year]
growth = ((end - start) / start * 100)[start >= 20].dropna()
fastest_area, fastest_growth = growth.idxmax(), growth.max()

# Survival of new venues (Kaplan-Meier), in years
key = ["property_id", "trading_name"]
spells = venues.groupby(key)["census_year"].agg(["min", "max"]).reset_index()
spells = spells[spells["min"] > first_year]            # only venues whose opening we observe
spells["years"] = spells["max"] - spells["min"] + 1    # years seen open
spells["closed"] = spells["max"] < latest_year         # still open in the latest census = not closed yet

survival = 1.0
median_lifespan = None
survival_5 = None
for d in sorted(spells["years"].unique()):
    at_risk = (spells["years"] >= d).sum()
    closed_now = ((spells["years"] == d) & spells["closed"]).sum()
    survival *= 1 - closed_now / at_risk
    if d <= 5:
        survival_5 = survival                          # share still open after 5 years
    if median_lifespan is None and survival <= 0.5:
        median_lifespan = d                            # half of new venues have closed by now

# Share of today's venues in the CBD
cbd_share = (latest["area"] == "Melbourne (CBD)").mean() * 100

# Share of today's venues that opened in the last 5 years
key = ["property_id", "trading_name"]
first_seen = venues.groupby(key)["census_year"].min()
latest_first_seen = latest.set_index(key).index.map(first_seen)
new_share = (latest_first_seen > latest_year - 5).mean() * 100     

def style(fig):
    """Shared clean styling for all charts."""
    fig.update_layout(
        template="simple_white",
        margin=dict(l=50, r=20, t=20, b=50),     # a bit more room for larger axis text
        legend=dict(
            orientation="v",                      # one item per line
            yanchor="top", y=0.98,                # top-left corner, inside the chart
            xanchor="left", x=0.02,
            bgcolor="rgba(255,255,255,0.85)",     # white background so lines stay readable
            title_text="",
            font=dict(size=11),
        ),
        font=dict(size=13),
    )
    fig.update_xaxes(
        title_font=dict(size=18),                 # x-axis title, e.g. "Census year"
        tickfont=dict(size=14),                   # x-axis tick labels, e.g. 2010
    )
    fig.update_yaxes(
        title_font=dict(size=18),                 # y-axis title, e.g. "Venues"
        tickfont=dict(size=14),                   # y-axis tick labels
    )
    return fig

def area_chart(include_cbd=True):
    """Venues per year by area; optionally without the CBD."""
    data = venues if include_cbd else venues[venues["area"] != "Melbourne (CBD)"]
    by_area = data.groupby(["census_year", "area"]).size().reset_index(name="venues")

    # Order areas by their average number of venues (highest first),
    # so the hover box lists the busiest area at the top
    area_order = by_area.groupby("area")["venues"].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).index.tolist()

    fig = px.line(
        by_area, x="census_year", y="venues", color="area",
        category_orders={"area": area_order},
        labels={"census_year": "Census year", "venues": "Number of venues", "area": "Area"},
    )
    style(fig)
    fig.update_layout(
        showlegend=False,          # no legend: names appear when you hover
        hovermode="x unified",     # one box listing all areas for the year
        hoverlabel=dict(font_size=14),
    )
    fig.update_traces(
        line=dict(width=2.5),   # thicker lines (default is 2)
        hovertemplate="<b>%{fullData.name}</b>: %{y}<extra></extra>",
    )

    return fig
```

```{python}
#| title: "Number of venues by area (2002–2024)"
#| width: 45%
from IPython.display import HTML

fig = area_chart(include_cbd=True)
_ = fig.update_traces(hoverinfo="none", hovertemplate=None)   # we draw our own hover box below
chart_html = fig.to_html(
    full_html=False, include_plotlyjs="cdn", div_id="area-chart",
    default_height="100%", default_width="100%",
    config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False},
)

# A regular web-page button that hides/shows the CBD line,
# plus our own hover box that sorts the areas by their value in the hovered year
HTML(f"""
<div class="area-chart-wrap">
  <button class="cbd-toggle" onclick="toggleCBD(this)">Hide CBD</button>
  <div class="area-chart-plot" style="position:relative;">
    {chart_html}
    <div id="area-hover" style="position:absolute; display:none; pointer-events:none; z-index:10;
         background:white; border:1px solid #DDDDDD; border-radius:4px; padding:6px 8px;
         box-shadow:0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.15); line-height:1.35; white-space:nowrap;"></div>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
function toggleCBD(btn) {{
  var gd = document.getElementById("area-chart");
  var idx = [];
  gd.data.forEach(function (t, i) {{ if (t.name === "Melbourne (CBD)") idx.push(i); }});
  var hide = btn.dataset.hidden !== "1";
  Plotly.restyle(gd, {{visible: !hide}}, idx);
  Plotly.relayout(gd, {{"yaxis.autorange": true}});
  btn.dataset.hidden = hide ? "1" : "0";
  btn.textContent = hide ? "Show CBD" : "Hide CBD";
}}

(function () {{
  var gd = document.getElementById("area-chart");
  var box = document.getElementById("area-hover");

  function attach() {{
    if (!gd.on) {{ return setTimeout(attach, 100); }}

    gd.on("plotly_hover", function (ev) {{
      // Sort the areas from highest to lowest value in this year
      var pts = ev.points.filter(function (p) {{ return p.data.visible !== false; }})
                         .sort(function (a, b) {{ return b.y - a.y; }});
      if (!pts.length) return;
      var cw = gd.offsetWidth;
      box.style.fontSize = (cw < 380 ? 10 : (cw < 520 ? 11 : 13)) + "px";
      box.innerHTML = "<b>" + pts[0].x + "</b><br>" + pts.map(function (p) {{
        return '<span style="color:' + p.data.line.color + '">&#9644;</span> <b>' +
               p.data.name + "</b>: " + p.y.toLocaleString();
      }}).join("<br>");

      // Place the box next to the hovered year, on whichever side has room
      var px = gd._fullLayout.xaxis.l2p(pts[0].x) + gd._fullLayout._size.l;
      box.style.display = "block";
      var left = px + 12;
      if (left + box.offsetWidth > cw) left = px - 12 - box.offsetWidth;
      box.style.left = Math.max(0, left) + "px";
      box.style.top = gd._fullLayout._size.t + "px";
    }});
    gd.on("plotly_unhover", function () {{ box.style.display = "none"; }});
  }}
  attach();
}})();
</script>
""")
```

```{python}
#| title: "Open venues by area and type (2024)"
#| width: 45%
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# 1. How many venues of each type are open in each area (latest census)
now = venues[venues["census_year"] == latest_year]
counts = now.groupby(["area", "type"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
counts = counts.drop(columns=["Other", "Entertainment, sport & culture"], errors="ignore")   # leave out less informative groups

# 2. Five-year survival of new venues for each area and type (Kaplan-Meier)
key = ["property_id", "trading_name"]
first_rows = venues.sort_values("census_year").groupby(key).first().reset_index()
spells_h = venues.groupby(key)["census_year"].agg(["min", "max"]).reset_index()
spells_h = spells_h.merge(first_rows[key + ["area", "type"]], on=key)   # area and type in the opening year
spells_h = spells_h[spells_h["min"] > first_year]                         # only venues whose opening we observe
spells_h["years"] = spells_h["max"] - spells_h["min"] + 1
spells_h["closed"] = spells_h["max"] < latest_year

def survival_at(d, horizon=5):
    """Kaplan-Meier estimate of the share still open after `horizon` years."""
    s = 1.0
    for t in sorted(d["years"].unique()):
        if t > horizon:
            break
        at_risk = (d["years"] >= t).sum()
        closed_now = ((d["years"] == t) & d["closed"]).sum()
        s *= 1 - closed_now / at_risk
    return s * 100

surv = {
    (a, t): (survival_at(d), len(d))
    for (a, t), d in spells_h.groupby(["area", "type"])
}

# Order: busiest areas at the top, most common types on the left
area_order = counts.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).index.tolist()
type_order = counts.sum(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index.tolist()
counts = counts.loc[area_order, type_order]

# Short column labels (the full name still shows in the hover box)
SHORT = {
    "Cafés & restaurants": "Cafés &<br>restaurants",
    "Takeaway & catering": "Takeaway &<br>catering",
    "Pubs, bars & clubs": "Pubs &<br>bars",
    "Accommodation": "Hotels",
    "Bakeries & food shops": "Bakeries &<br>food shops",
    "Entertainment, sport & culture": "Leisure",
    "Other": "Other",
}

# Hover text: number open now, plus 5-year survival where there are enough new venues
hover = [
    [
        f"<b>{t}</b> in <b>{a}</b><br>Open in {latest_year}: {counts.loc[a, t]:,}"
        + (
            f"<br>Still open after 5 years: {surv[(a, t)][0]:.0f}% (of {surv[(a, t)][1]:,} new venues)"
            if (a, t) in surv and surv[(a, t)][1] >= 20 else ""
        )
        for t in type_order
    ]
    for a in area_order
]

fig = go.Figure(go.Heatmap(
    z=np.log1p(counts.values),            # log scale for colour, so smaller areas still show shades
    x=type_order, y=area_order,
    text=counts.values, texttemplate="%{text}",
    textfont=dict(size=12),
    customdata=hover, hovertemplate="%{customdata}<extra></extra>",
    colorscale=[[0, "#FFFFFF"], [1, BLUE]], showscale=False,
    xgap=2, ygap=2,
))
_ = style(fig)
_ = fig.update_layout(hoverlabel=dict(font_size=13), margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10))
_ = fig.update_xaxes(
    side="top", tickangle=0,
    tickvals=type_order, ticktext=[SHORT.get(t, t) for t in type_order],
    tickfont=dict(size=13), showline=False, automargin=True,
    ticks="outside", ticklen=6, tickcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
)
_ = fig.update_yaxes(
    autorange="reversed", tickfont=dict(size=12), showline=False,
    ticks="outside", ticklen=6, tickcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
)
fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False})
```

```{python}
#| title: "Open and closed venues by area (2002–2024)"
#| width: 50%
import folium
from folium.plugins import Fullscreen
from branca.element import MacroElement
from jinja2 import Template

OPEN_COLOUR = "#D62828"     # teal: still open
CLOSED_COLOUR = "#9E9E9E"   # neutral grey: closed

# One row per venue across all census years: when it was first and last seen
key = ["property_id", "trading_name"]
history = (
    venues.sort_values("census_year")
    .groupby(key)
    .agg(
        first_year=("census_year", "min"),
        last_year=("census_year", "max"),
        area=("area", "last"),
        latitude=("latitude", "last"),
        longitude=("longitude", "last"),
        seats=("seats", "last"),
    )
    .reset_index()
    .dropna(subset=["latitude", "longitude"])
)
history["is_open"] = history["last_year"] == latest_year
history["status"] = history.apply(
    lambda r: f"Open in {latest_year}" if r["is_open"] else f"Closed (last seen {int(r['last_year'])})",
    axis=1,
)
history["years"] = history["first_year"].astype(int).astype(str) + "–" + history["last_year"].astype(int).astype(str)
history["seats"] = history["seats"].astype(int)

def convex_hull(points):
    """Smallest convex shape around a set of (lon, lat) points (monotone chain)."""
    pts = sorted(set(points))
    if len(pts) < 3:
        return []
    def cross(o, a, b):
        return (a[0] - o[0]) * (b[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[0] - o[0])
    lower, upper = [], []
    for p in pts:
        while len(lower) >= 2 and cross(lower[-2], lower[-1], p) <= 0:
            lower.pop()
        lower.append(p)
    for p in reversed(pts):
        while len(upper) >= 2 and cross(upper[-2], upper[-1], p) <= 0:
            upper.pop()
        upper.append(p)
    hull = lower[:-1] + upper[:-1]
    return hull + [hull[0]]

AREA_PALETTE = [
    "#4E79A7",  # blue
    "#F28E2B",  # orange
    "#E15759",  # red
    "#59A14F",  # green
    "#EDC948",  # yellow
    "#7B4FA0",  # purple
    "#FF8FB1",  # pink
    "#9C6B3F",  # brown
    "#B8D433",  # lime
    "#1F2F7A",  # navy
    "#7A7A1F",  # olive
    "#7A1F3D",  # maroon
]

def area_layer(data):
    """A coloured, see-through shape around the venues of each area."""
    features = []
    for i, (area, d) in enumerate(data.groupby("area")):
        hull = convex_hull(list(zip(d["longitude"], d["latitude"])))
        if hull:
            features.append({
                "type": "Feature",
                "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [hull]},
                "properties": {"Area": area, "colour": AREA_PALETTE[i % len(AREA_PALETTE)]},
            })
    return folium.GeoJson(
        {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features},
        name="Areas",
        style_function=lambda f: {
            "color": f["properties"]["colour"], "weight": 1, "opacity": 0.6,
            "fillColor": f["properties"]["colour"], "fillOpacity": 0.15,
        },
        tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(fields=["Area"], labels=False, sticky=True),
    )

def venue_layer(data, name, colour, radius, opacity):
    """One clickable layer of venues: a circle per venue, popup with details."""
    features = [
        {
            "type": "Feature",
            "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [r.longitude, r.latitude]},
            "properties": {
                "Venue": r.trading_name, "Area": r.area, "Seats": r.seats,
                "Status": r.status, "In census": r.years,
            },
        }
        for r in data.itertuples()
    ]
    return folium.GeoJson(
        {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features},
        name=name,
        marker=folium.CircleMarker(radius=radius, weight=0, fill=True, fill_opacity=opacity),
        style_function=lambda f, c=colour: {"fillColor": c, "color": c},
        tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(fields=["Venue"], labels=False),
        popup=folium.GeoJsonPopup(fields=["Venue", "Area", "Seats", "Status", "In census"]),
    )

m = folium.Map(
    location=[-37.8136, 144.9631], zoom_start=14,
    tiles=None, prefer_canvas=True, control_scale=True,
    width="100%", height="100%",
)
_ = folium.TileLayer(
    tiles="https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Canvas/World_Light_Gray_Base/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
    attr="Tiles © Esri — Esri, HERE, Garmin, © OpenStreetMap contributors",
    name="Light grey map", max_native_zoom=16, max_zoom=19,
).add_to(m)
_ = folium.TileLayer("OpenStreetMap", name="Street map").add_to(m)

# Layers are drawn in this order: areas at the bottom, closed venues, then open venues on top
areas = area_layer(history)
_ = areas.add_to(m)
venue_layers = []
for subset, name, colour, radius, opacity in [
    (history[~history["is_open"]], "Closed", CLOSED_COLOUR, 3, 0.5),
    (history[history["is_open"]], f"Open in {latest_year}", OPEN_COLOUR, 4, 0.85),
]:
    if len(subset):                       # skip a layer if it has no venues
        layer = venue_layer(subset, name, colour, radius, opacity)
        _ = layer.add_to(m)
        venue_layers.append(layer)

# Hovering over an area (or one of its venues) highlights its venues and fades the rest
highlight = MacroElement()
highlight._template = Template("""
{% macro script(this, kwargs) %}
(function () {
    var areas = """ + areas.get_name() + """;
    var venueLayers = [""" + ", ".join(l.get_name() for l in venue_layers) + """];
    var current = null, timer = null;

    venueLayers.forEach(function (lyr) {
        lyr.eachLayer(function (c) {
            c._base = {r: c.getRadius(), o: c.options.fillOpacity};
            c.on("mouseover", function () { show(c.feature.properties.Area); });
            c.on("mouseout", later);
        });
    });

    function paint(area) {
        venueLayers.forEach(function (lyr) {
            lyr.eachLayer(function (c) {
                if (area === null) {
                    c.setRadius(c._base.r); c.setStyle({fillOpacity: c._base.o});
                } else if (c.feature.properties.Area === area) {
                    c.setRadius(c._base.r + 2); c.setStyle({fillOpacity: 1});
                } else {
                    c.setRadius(c._base.r); c.setStyle({fillOpacity: 0.08});
                }
            });
        });
            areas.eachLayer(function (p) {
            var on = p.feature.properties.Area === area;
            p.setStyle({fillOpacity: on ? 0.45 : 0.15, weight: on ? 3 : 1, opacity: on ? 1 : 0.6});
        });
    }
    function show(area) {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        if (area !== current) { current = area; paint(area); }
    }
    function later() {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        timer = setTimeout(function () { current = null; paint(null); }, 80);
    }
    areas.eachLayer(function (p) {
        p.on("mouseover", function () { show(p.feature.properties.Area); });
        p.on("mouseout", later);
    });
})();
{% endmacro %}
""")
_ = m.add_child(highlight)

_ = folium.LayerControl(collapsed=False).add_to(m)
_ = Fullscreen().add_to(m)

# Show the map so that it fills the whole card
from html import escape
from IPython.display import HTML
map_html = m.get_root().render()
HTML(f'<iframe srcdoc="{escape(map_html)}" style="width:100%; height:100%; border:none;"></iframe>')
```

## About {height=600px}

:::

::: {.card title="About this dashboard" width="50%"}
**Data**

- City of Melbourne, Census of Land Use and Employment (CLUE): "Café, restaurant, bistro seats", census years 2002–2024
- Covers all venues with seating in the City of Melbourne municipality (CBD and inner suburbs)

**Method**

- **Venues:** Each business at a given address is counted once per census year.
- **Venue types:** Industry codes grouped into broader categories.
- **Median venue lifespan:** Years until half of the venues opened after 2002 have closed (Kaplan–Meier estimate)
- **Five-year survival** (venue type chart, on hover): Share of venues still open five years after opening; shown where at least 20 venues opened.
- **Map:** *open* means present in the 2024 census; area shapes are approximate.

**Limitations**

- City of Melbourne only, not greater Melbourne
- A venue that changes name or moves counts as a closure plus a new opening, so lifespans are conservative.

**Credits**

Built with Python, pandas, Plotly, Folium and Quarto. Data licensed CC BY (City of Melbourne). Map tiles © Esri and © OpenStreetMap contributors.
:::
